cars.specification_market: Japan-market 2003 CPV35 Skyline Coupe 350GT, Nissan Heritage Collection no. 497 reference. Its VQ35DE table gives 3498 cc, 206 kW at 6200 rpm and 363 Nm at 4800 rpm; native kW/Nm are retained, not substituted with American G35 horsepower/torque or later Rev-Up/HR values. This museum entry does not identify its transmission or detailed equipment grade, so neither five-speed automatic nor six-speed manual is asserted as a technical field. In particular, the history paragraph’s eight-speed transmission belongs to the separate 350GT-8 sedan, not this coupe. Count V35/CPV35 and the export G35 badge once across bodies, gearboxes, packages and years; no second Infiniti record is added.
cars.summary: The V35 Skyline Coupe / Infiniti G35 brought Nissan’s front-midship V6 architecture to a distinctive four-seat sports coupe. The export G35 coupe shared Motor Trend’s 2003 Car of the Year award with its saloon sibling, giving this generation an established performance-car significance beyond its Skyline badge.

cars.generation: Original C4 S4/S6/S6 plus sporting-road family
cars.variant: S6 plus saloon — October 1996 German factory technical reference
cars.specification_market: C4 S6 plus saloon, German offering as of October 1996, original Audi factory technical sheet preserved by the Internet Archive. Select the left sedan column: 5.6-second 0–100 km/h and 1695 kg unladen weight, not the Avant’s 5.7 seconds/1745 kg. The common engine table gives 4172 cc V8, four overhead camshafts/four valves per cylinder, 11.6:1, 240 kW at 6500 rpm and 400 Nm at 3500 rpm under 80/1269/EEC. Native kW/Nm are retained; 326 PS is not mechanical bhp. Six-speed manual, Torsen centre differential and dual-mass flywheel are explicit; a secondary single-mass claim is not adopted. Performance and governed 250 km/h are factory claims. Count the C4 S4/S6/S6 plus sporting-road lineage once across names, engines, saloon/Avant bodies and years; ordinary A6 trim does not create another record.
cars.summary: The C4 S6 plus was quattro GmbH’s first complete high-performance model as a vehicle manufacturer, preceding its later RS programmes. Its reworked V8, six-speed manual and permanent quattro make it a substantive milestone in Audi Sport’s road-car engineering history.
